SectionObject.Title: Public transport
SectionObject.Text1: Here you can see where buses and trams in public transport are located in real time. The same data used in the model is used for traffic information at stops and in apps. Can you catch the next bus?

SectionObject.Title: Traffic noise
SectionObject.Text1:
Here you can see how central Norrköping is affected by traffic noise. The illustration shows how much surface area the noise spreads at the maximum level for each location. The railway emits the most noise.
All cities with more than 100,000 inhabitants have an obligation to make calculations for traffic noise at least every five years. The calculations are made on the basis of many different parameters such as traffic flows, the design of the road, adjacent buildings and speeds. The noise level is calculated at the facade, i.e. outside the house. How the noise level is perceived inside the house largely depends on how the house is built, how well insulated the house is and what windows there are.
How do you experience traffic noise where you live?

SectionObject.Title: Extreme rainfall 100-year flow
SectionObject.Text1:
A 100-year rainfall occurs statistically once every hundred years. The highlighted areas on the model are the areas that are worst affected by extreme rain.
When the municipality plans for new buildings, they take flood risks into account and set requirements for various measures. It could, for example, be about raising the ground level and foundation level when building new houses. But it is at least as important to ensure that large amounts of water have somewhere to go.
One of the measures the municipality is working on is to create submerged surfaces in parks and natural areas. By making submerged surfaces in suitable places and creating them lower than surrounding buildings or roads, the water can collect there instead of causing flooding in places where it causes damage.

SectionObject.Title: Sea level rise
SectionObject.Text1: Seas are rising and will continue to do so for a long time due to global warming. If warming is limited, sea level rise will also be less. There are plans for dike constructions and a lock in Kvarsebo to meet a higher sea level.

SectionObject.Title: Tree
SectionObject.Text1:
Here you can see where there are trees in the city. Trees in urban environments are important for our well-being. They contribute to greenery and improve the polluted air coming from cars and factories. The trees in the city also have a temperature equalizing effect by using solar energy for their growth. At the same time, the foliage provides shade and coolness in cities during hot summer days. In the case of rainfall, they can reduce the load on the city's sewage system by absorbing large amounts of water. Trees also act as a node in a green network in the city. They favor biological diversity and offer habitat for birds and habitat for a number of plants, mosses, insects and lichens.
Do you think Norrköping is a green city?

SectionObject.Title: Workplace density
SectionObject.Text1: Here you can see where there are most workplaces in Norrköping today. As you can see, it is in central Norrköping and at Vrinnevisjukhuset that there is the densest number of workplaces. But if we look ahead to 2050, we can see that the party workplaces can be found in Butängen, on Sylten and in Norra Himmelstalund.

SectionObject.Title: Housing density
SectionObject.Text1: Where do most people live in Norrköping? The model has taken into account the city's barriers and calculated how many residents you reach within 250 meters of each point. The analysis can be used to more accurately calculate data when, for example, planning public transport and school places.

SectionObject.Title: Building types
SectionObject.Text1:
Here you can see how the distribution looks between housing and businesses.
Over the years, there have been different ideals for how a city should be built. From 1945 to 1965, Norrköping was to a large extent a mixed city where housing, workplaces and trade were relatively close. Most people went to work on foot or by bicycle and did their shopping in their neighborhood. From the mid-60s, the car struck again on a large scale and the city was planned from a completely new perspective. Center malls grew, residential areas were built outside the city center and streets were widened to make room for the car's progress. In recent years, the pursuit of a mixed city has gained momentum again and the concept of the 15-minute city, i.e. the ability to reach what you need within 15 minutes from your home, has become increasingly popular.
Based on the distribution of homes and businesses today - do you think that Norrköping is a mixed city?

SectionObject.Title: Lighting
SectionObject.Text1:
Did you know that there are around 28,000 lighting poles in the municipality of Norrköping?
In the municipality, all lighting poles are documented in a map. In order to update the map, the municipality sometimes needs to go out to measure where poles are or use drawings for new construction. With the help of the new AI technology developed within the SimStad project, an AI (artificial intelligence) can itself scan an area and classify different types of objects, which both makes the information more detailed and significantly easier to keep up to date.
On the model you can see where there are lighting poles and how large an area the light covers. For the municipality, this is important in order to be able to analyze where new lighting is needed in future planning and to be able to look after the existing lighting.

SectionObject.Title: Urban development areas
SectionObject.Text1:
Areas where more extensive urban development is planned or implemented in Norrköping are marked here right now. Did you know that there will be around 3,000 new homes in the Inner Harbour? Or that the whole of Butängen should be converted into a part of the inner city in connection with the construction of the Ostlänken high-speed railway?
On the model, you can also see that the Sylten area will get a facelift in the future and that Norrköping's western neighborhoods will grow.

SectionObject.Title: Year of construction
SectionObject.Text1:
By looking at the year of construction, we can see how the city has developed over time and where new construction has been added in recent years.
Around the turn of the last century, Norrköping was in a boom. The textile industry grew and so did the city. In the middle of the 20th century, the textile crisis hit and production in the central industrial area gradually decreased.
Despite the decline of the industries, investments were made in new housing during the 60s and 70s. Older homes were demolished to make way for new, more modern ones. But while the demolitions continued, the city stagnated and the need for new housing quickly diminished. This led to many demolished plots and blocks that were not developed. Only around the turn of the last millennium did these gaps gradually begin to be filled with new housing, workplaces, restaurants, commerce, etc.
